title: Simulation run
description:
One execution of a physics solver, with everything needed to reproduce or distrust it.

The governing rule from the architecture: never show an impressive simulation without provenance. A stress plot with no mesh size, no solver version and no convergence history is a picture, not a result — and a picture that looks like a result is worse than no picture.

The shape is informed by surrogate-accelerated design pipelines such as NovaTurbo, where a fast neural surrogate proposes and a real solver confirms. That workflow only stays honest if a surrogate estimate can never be mistaken for a solved field, which is why `fidelity` is required and why a surrogate result carries its own calibration record.

campaign_id.description: Groups runs belonging to one design study, so a Pareto front can be traced to the sweep that produced it.

fidelity.description: The single most important field. `surrogate` output is a prediction from a trained model and must never be rendered or reported as a solved field; `analytical` is a closed-form cycle estimate; `high_fidelity` is a converged solve. Confusing these is how a design review approves a part that was never actually simulated.

status.description: `diverged` is a result, not an absence of one, and is retained: a divergence at a particular operating point is often the most informative outcome of a sweep.

node_id.description: Fabric node that ran it. A result that cannot be attributed to hardware cannot be reproduced on it.

model_revision.description: Exactly which geometry was solved. A result whose input geometry cannot be recovered is not reproducible, however good the solver was.

generator.description: What produced the geometry, e.g. a parametric CAD module and its version.

parameters.description: The design and operating point, each value with its unit. This is what a sweep varies and what a Pareto point is indexed by.

version.description: Exact version. Solver releases change results; a comparison across versions that does not say so is not a comparison.

configuration_sha256.description: Digest of the full case setup, so two runs can be proven to have used identical configuration.

turbulence_model.description: e.g. k-omega-SST, Spalart-Allmaras. Reported because it changes the answer more than most parameters do.

mesh.description: Discretization quality. Reported for every field solve: results are only meaningful relative to the mesh that produced them.

y_plus_mean.description: Wall resolution for turbulent solves. Outside the range the chosen wall treatment assumes, the near-wall answer is not trustworthy regardless of convergence.

independence_study.description: Evidence that the answer stopped changing as the mesh refined. Its absence does not invalidate a run, but a design decision resting on a run without one should say so.

convergence.description: Whether the solve actually converged, in numbers. A `converged` status with residuals that plateaued three orders too high is a run that should be read as `diverged`.

monitored_quantity_drift.description: Change in the reported quantity over the final iterations. The honest convergence check: residuals can fall while the answer still moves.

results.description: Scalar outputs, each with unit and uncertainty where known.

fields.description: Field outputs available for overlay on the geometry — pressure, velocity, temperature, von Mises stress.

surrogate.description: Present only when fidelity is `surrogate`. A prediction is admissible in a design loop precisely because it is cheap, and dangerous for the same reason; recording which model produced it, and how it was calibrated, is what keeps it from being quoted as a solve.

calibrated_against.description: `uncalibrated` is permitted and must be surfaced. An uncalibrated surrogate is a hypothesis generator, not an evaluator.

in_training_domain.description: Whether this operating point lies inside the range the surrogate was trained on. Extrapolation is where surrogates fail silently, so it is recorded per run rather than assumed.

validation_state.description: How much the result has actually earned. Ascending: a converged run is only `self_consistent` until something outside it agrees.

optimization.description: Set when the run is a point in a multi-objective study.

safety_review.description: Gate between a simulation and anything physical. A result may inform a design, but a part that will carry load or a patch that will run on a controller requires an explicit human acceptance recorded here — a converged solve is not authorization.

allOf.$comment: A surrogate result must always say which model produced it and how that model was calibrated.
A converged solve must report how it converged. Otherwise the status is an assertion.
